title: Know what to do when something breaks
summary: Things will go wrong in live service. Agree in advance how the team will spot, fix and communicate problems, and how you will learn from them without blame.

beginner: Agree what counts as an incident, and how serious each level is.
Agree who is on call, how they are contacted and who leads when an incident happens.
Decide who tells users and stakeholders, and prepare simple message templates.
Make sure there is a way to roll back or switch off a feature quickly.
After each serious incident, hold a blameless review: what happened, why, and what you will change.
intermediate: Define incident severity levels and response times.
Agree on-call, incident lead and communication roles.
Check rollback and feature switch options.
Run blameless post-incident reviews and track actions.
experienced: Rehearse incidents so the process works under pressure.
Track incident trends and feed them into the roadmap.
Agree public status page and customer communication rules.
Build a culture where people report problems early without fear.

canDelegateTo.task: Set up on-call, alerting and rollback

toolExamples.jira: Use an incident issue type with severity, timeline and actions.
toolExamples.confluence: Use a post-incident review template and link actions to the backlog.
toolExamples.github: Document rollback steps in the repository so anyone on call can follow them.

pitfalls: Working it out during the first incident
Blaming individuals, so people hide problems
Fixing the symptom and not the cause

leaderView.good: Teams know in advance how to spot, fix and communicate problems, and learn from each incident.
ask: Who's on call, and how do users hear about problems?
What did we change after the last incident?
signs: Incidents are handled differently every time.
Reviews look for someone to blame.

sources.title: Postmortem culture: learning from failure (Google SRE book)
